definitions.explanation: The physical force used to pull or tow something, such as a vehicle or load.
The ability of a person, organization, or idea to draw others along and lead progress, used metaphorically.

examples.japanese: このエンジンは{牽引力|けんいんりょく}が{強|つよ}い。
examples.english: This engine has strong pulling power.

examples.japanese: {大型|おおがた}トラックには{十分|じゅうぶん}な{牽引力|けんいんりょく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
{路面|ろめん}が{凍結|とうけつ}すると{牽引力|けんいんりょく}が{大幅|おおはば}に{低下|ていか}する。
examples.english: When the road surface freezes, traction drops significantly.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}のリーダーシップが{改革|かいかく}の{牽引力|けんいんりょく}になった。
examples.english: His leadership became the driving force of the reform.

examples.japanese: IT{産業|さんぎょう}が{経済|けいざい}{成長|せいちょう}の{牽引力|けんいんりょく}を{担|にな}っている。
examples.english: The IT industry is serving as the driving force of economic growth.

examples.japanese: {新興|しんこう}{市場|しじょう}が{世界|せかい}{経済|けいざい}の{牽引力|けんいんりょく}として{注目|ちゅうもく}されている。
examples.english: Emerging markets are drawing attention as a driving force for the global economy.

notes:
Composed of {牽引|けんいん} (towing/pulling) + {力|りょく} (force/power). The physical meaning (sense 1) is used in automotive and engineering contexts, while the figurative meaning (sense 2) is common in business and political discourse.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {牽引力|けんいんりょく}が{強|つよ}い: to have strong pulling power
- {牽引力|けんいんりょく}を{発揮|はっき}する: to exert traction/driving force
- {牽引力|けんいんりょく}を{担|にな}う: to serve as a driving force
- {牽引力|けんいんりょく}が{低下|ていか}する: traction/momentum drops

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {推進力|すいしんりょく}: propulsive force; driving power — pushes from behind, while {牽引力|けんいんりょく} pulls from the front
- {原動力|げんどうりょく}: motive force; prime mover — emphasizes the origin of energy rather than the direction
- {求心力|きゅうしんりょく}: centripetal force; power to attract — emphasizes drawing people/things to a center
